definition: A schematic symbol is the standardized logical graphic used to represent a component or electrical function on a schematic.
A footprint is the PCB pad, hole, courtyard, and placement pattern assigned to a specific component package.
A pad is a conductive land on a PCB used to connect a component terminal, via, or test connection to copper.
A pin is a logical terminal on a schematic component that connects the component to a net.
A footprint pad is a numbered or named physical connection point in a PCB footprint.
A simulation terminal is the node connection used by a simulation model and may require explicit mapping to a component pin.
A pin mapping explicitly links a component pin to its footprint pad and simulation-model terminal.
A net is a named electrical connection shared by two or more pins, pads, or conductive board features.
A wire is a schematic connection line that electrically joins pins and other schematic connection objects.
A junction is a schematic connection point showing that intersecting wires are electrically joined.
A no-connect flag marks a schematic pin as intentionally left unconnected.
A net label assigns a name to a schematic connection so separated drawing locations can represent the same electrical net.
A ground symbol identifies a designated reference or return net in a schematic and does not by itself represent a purchased physical component.
A power symbol identifies a named supply net such as VCC, VDD, or +3V3 without representing a physical inventory item by itself.
A bus is a grouped representation of multiple related signals or nets used to simplify schematic or logic views.
A passive pin is a terminal type that does not assert power or digital-drive behavior during topology-only electrical-rule checks.
A power input pin is a terminal type intended to receive electrical power from a suitable source.
A power output pin is a terminal type intended to provide electrical power to other parts of a circuit.
A digital input pin is a terminal type intended to receive a digital logic signal.
A digital output pin is a terminal type intended to drive a digital logic signal.
An open-drain pin is a digital output type that can actively pull a net low but normally requires an external pull-up to produce a high state.
